newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand plans measures to help ailing bourse.
newsitem.headline: Thailand plans measures to help ailing bourse.

text.p: Bank of Thailand assistant governor Siri Ganjarerndee said Thai authorities will announce measures on Monday to help support the battered stock market.

Those measures include the issue of 5.0 billion baht ($192 million) bonds by Securities Finance Corp (SFC) which will use the funds to purchase margin loans from securities companies, Siri told reporters on Friday.
"The funds from the bond issue might not be sufficient (to support the stock market). There will be other measures which will be announced on Monday," he said.
Siri is also the advisor of the SFC which was established last year as a lending centre for Thailand securities companies.

Thailand's bourse has plunged to eight-year lows this week, hit by a combination of worries about slowing economic growth, a fragile currency, high interest rates, cash-strapped financial and property sectors, and concerns that government efforts to improve the situation may not be enough. ($1 = 26 baht)
